summary: v2.0 upgrade tested: 26 engines + SSE + canon flow + OG PNG + marketplace + webhooks + safety. Backend 18/20 pytests pass. Frontend: dashboard SSE run (26 engines + result JSON), marketplace anon/admin, public /public/{id} page, control deck 26 cells + WebhookManager (admin), debug all 26 green — ALL pass. Two backend failures share one root cause: the top-level /canon/{id} route is served by the React frontend (not FastAPI) because the K8s ingress routes only /api/* to backend; result is HTML 200 but it's the SPA shell, not the server-rendered canon page with OG meta. Critical to fix before Day-1 social shares.

critical.issue: Route registered on FastAPI app (not under /api router) is unreachable via public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. K8s ingress proxies only /api/* to port 8001. Public URL returns the React index.html (200) for /canon/{id}, so og:image / og:url meta + crawler share previews + entire Layer-3 'public CDN substitute' feature is broken. Verified: localhost:8001/canon/<id> → backend HTML (or 403/404); public /canon/<id> → React SPA shell. Move route to @api.get('/canon/{asset_id}') (under /api) or configure ingress to passthrough.

minor.issue: Admin approve does NOT enforce Safety engine — assets with safe:false (e.g. seed 'kill someone') still enter canon, generate /canon page, and render their unsafe seed verbatim in the public HTML. Marketplace listing is correctly blocked. Recommend: reject approval if engines.Safety.safe == false (or require explicit override flag).

rca of the issue: Root cause: FastAPI declares @app.get('/canon/{asset_id}') at the top-level app, not on the /api APIRouter. The Kubernetes ingress in this environment is configured to forward only /api/* to the backend pod; anything else (including /canon/*) goes to the React frontend at port 3000. The frontend's React Router has no '/canon/:id' route (only '/canon' for CanonVault), so the SPA shell is served as 200 with default React index.html, masquerading as a successful response. Reproduction: curl http://localhost:8001/canon/<any> → backend response (200/403/404 depending on canon state); curl <PUBLIC_URL>/canon/<any> → React SPA HTML (200, contains 'A product of emergent.sh' meta, no og:image meta). Mitigation: move the route to api.get('/canon/{asset_id}') (under the /api router) — or expose it at /api/public/canon/{id}.html — and update PUBLIC_BASE_URL + the Open-Server-Page frontend link to use that path. After fix, re-run pytest to confirm both failing tests pass.
